description:
Found by the cold review of fz-5xp.31. PRE-EXISTING (the code path is untouched
by that change), and trivially reachable:

    fn main(), do: dbg(-3.0)

  interp -> -3.0
  run    -> panic: cannot read raw i64 from non-integer value
  build  -> the same

CAUSE. `Prim::UnOp(Neg)` in `src/compiler2/native_codegen/prim.rs` unconditionally
does `as_raw_i64` then `ineg` -- there is no float arm, so `fn_ctx.rs`'s
`as_raw_i64` aborts on a float. The interpreter negates by value and is fine.

WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN "someday": fz-5xp.15 is Float formatting. Its oracle
will compare `Float.to_string(-3.0)` and friends against Elixir, and every
negative-float fixture in the epic from here on will hit this on two of the
three doors. It also means `behavior/extern_float_lanes` could not use a
negative input even though negatives are exactly where a sign-conversion bug in
the marshalling would show.

DONE = `-3.0`, `-x` for a float `x`, and a float negation in a larger
expression all agree on interp, run and build, with a fixture that covers a
negative literal, a negated float variable, and a negated float returned from a
call. Check `UnOp(Neg)`'s sibling operators at the same time -- if `Neg` had no
float arm, the others deserve a look.
title: [BUG] A negative float literal aborts run and build
